meta.title: Bingoo — Learn joyfully, grow every day
meta.description: Bingoo (bingoo.ai) is an online learning platform helping kids aged 6–15 master Math, Vietnamese and English through a personalized path, playful gamification and Bingoo, their learning buddy.

hero.title: Teach adaptively, and
hero.subtitle: Bingoo Open is a teaching toolkit for tutors, freelance teachers, learning centres and small schools: map what has to be learned, build lessons that fit, teach with interactive manipulatives, and measure with evidence you can check by hand.
hero.note: Runs on your own machine · No account · No per-seat pricing
hero.safe: A person approves what a child sees

frameworks.title: Each one usable on its own
frameworks.subtitle: Take the whole thing, or install one package and ignore the rest.

knowledge.name: Knowledge
knowledge.desc: A competency graph with prerequisites — what lets the system say "she cannot do this yet because she has not got that", instead of just marking an answer wrong.

pedagogy.name: Pedagogy
pedagogy.desc: Lesson plans carrying the misconceptions learners arrive with, concrete → pictorial → abstract representations, and what counts as success.

teaching.name: Teaching
teaching.desc: A lesson engine and 67 manipulatives: number lines, base-ten blocks, fraction bars, balance scales, circuits, coordinate grids.

content.name: Content
content.desc: Authoring and generation of items, six question types, an item bank with coverage tracking.

learning.name: Learning
learning.desc: Learner-facing modes, session flow, and evidence capture.

measure.title: Every number can explain itself
measure.subtitle: A number you cannot explain to a parent does not belong on a screen.

evidence.name: Evidence, not marks
evidence.desc: Every attempt becomes evidence with a timestamp and a source. Replay the log from scratch and the same number comes back.

rightTool.name: The right tool for each thing
rightTool.desc: Knowledge and procedures use Bayesian knowledge tracing and Elo. Skills are scored against rubrics by a person, because a machine grading a skill without a rubric is guessing.

disposition.name: Dispositions are never scored
disposition.desc: Habits are reported as observed frequencies with a confidence interval, and never mixed into an academic grade.

explain.name: Explainable
explain.desc: Any estimate produces the claim, the evidence behind it, the formula used, and what would have to change for it to read differently.

editions.title: Start where it fits
editions.subtitle: The open edition is the whole thing, not a trial. The other two exist for when you want them.

open.name: Bingoo Open
open.desc: You run it, on your own machine or your own server. The full authoring toolkit and the learn–teach apps. Data never leaves where you put it.

points.b: Works with any S3-compatible store, including MinIO on your laptop
points.c: Curricula in via CASE, evidence out via xAPI

cloud.name: Bingoo Cloud
cloud.desc: A hosted edition for places without a technical team. Adds higher-tier AI, automation, exam sittings and a parent portal.

points.c: Move to self-hosting whenever you like

network.name: Bingoo Network
network.desc: A competency record the learner owns, carried between schools and into a career — still there years later.

editions.note: Cloud and Network are commercial services from Bingoo.ai. The open edition needs neither to run in full.

transfer.title: Moving schools without starting over
transfer.subtitle: A learner on a national curriculum moves to an international one. The system compares the two and says immediately what is already done.

kept.name: Already there · kept
kept.desc: What has been mastered is recognised in the new curriculum. No relearning.

missing.name: Missing · scheduled
missing.desc: What the new standard expects and the learner has not met becomes the next path.

extra.name: Beyond · recorded
extra.desc: Advanced work the new curriculum does not need yet is recorded as a strength.

openness.title: You can leave whenever you want
openness.subtitle: Which is what makes staying mean something.

standards.name: Open standards
standards.desc: Curricula come in as CASE, evidence goes out as xAPI. You can take both the graph and the evidence with you.

swap.name: Swap providers by configuration
swap.desc: Every external service sits behind a port with swappable adapters. Changing provider is configuration, not a rewrite.

audit.name: Auditable
audit.desc: All of it is public. The mastery formulas can be read, re-run and argued with.

contribute.name: Contributable
contribute.desc: Apache-2.0, DCO sign-off, no CLA. Disagreement about the modelling counts as a contribution too.

cta.title: Running in ten minutes
cta.subtitle: Needs Node 22 and pnpm 9. The web app comes up with sample data, so you can click through a lesson before configuring anything.

safety.metaDescription: Bingoo puts kids' safety first — moderated content, no ads, parent controls, data privacy.
safety.title: Safety comes first
safety.subtitle: Bingoo is built so parents can feel completely at ease.

0.d: Every lesson and dynamic piece of content is reviewed before it reaches a child.

1.d: No ads, no external links, no distracting in-app purchases.

2.d: Set screen-time limits, follow activity, and manage your child's account.

3.d: Children's data is protected; we never sell information to third parties.

safety.note: Bingoo follows safety principles for children's content.

faq.metaDescription: Common questions parents ask about Bingoo — ages, safety, devices, pricing.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: What parents often ask about Bingoo.

0.a: Bingoo is an online learning platform for kids aged 6–15 that turns lessons into games, with a personalized path and Bingoo as a friendly buddy.

1.a: Content follows the curriculum for kids aged 6 to 15 and adapts its difficulty to each child's level.

2.a: Yes. Content is moderated, there are no ads, and parents get screen-time controls.

3.q: What devices can my child learn on?
3.a: Bingoo runs in the web browser, on tablets and phones — just sign in and pick up where you left off.

4.a: There's a Free plan to get started; Plus and Family unlock the full experience. See the Pricing page for details.

5.a: You can cancel anytime from your account settings — no fees, no strings attached.

authoring.title: Authoring
authoring.description: Pipeline map: framework → align → course shell → per-lesson plans → coverage. Each stage happens at a different time.
authoring.fwDesc: Describe a topic for the AI to generate a framework, or upload a curriculum/book PDF to extract one.
authoring.fwPromptPh: e.g. Grade 3 maths — basic fractions (recognise, compare, add/subtract same denominator)
authoring.fwApplied: Framework written to the competency graph
authoring.courseDesc: Write a course brief or upload a book (PDF). Lessons may only anchor to competencies that exist in the graph.
authoring.coursePromptPh: e.g. A 12-session course teaching fractions to grade 3, 35 minutes each
authoring.planFirst: Generate the plan first so content follows the pedagogy
authoring.dropLabel: Drag a PDF here, or click to choose
authoring.fwListDesc: Inspect detail, manage releases and the competency graph.
authoring.courseListDesc: Generated course shells — approve, publish or delete.
authoring.caseViewerIntro: This is {title} in CASE format — an open standard so other software (an LMS, a spreadsheet) can read this competency framework.
authoring.caseSelectHint: Select an objective to read its full statement and relationships — enough to review before you use the framework.
authoring.caseNoRelations: This objective has no declared links to others in the framework.
authoring.explainSelectHint: Click an item on the map to see what it is and why it's here.
authoring.explainFacets: Identifying marks — what makes this knowledge distinct from others
authoring.explainNoRelations: No links to other items in this framework.
authoring.explainDerived: Computed from the graph — not authored.
authoring.tbEmpty: No trace for this objective yet — import from a document or run the seed first.
authoring.tbDriftWarn: Re-checking today gives a DIFFERENT result than at review time — this needs re-reviewing.
authoring.tbSourceFoundBody: These exact words appear in the document you uploaded. This only confirms the knowledge IS in the document — not the learning order, nor that the AI read it correctly.
authoring.tbSourceUnverifiedTitle: AI quoted it, but the system couldn't find it
authoring.tbSourceUnverifiedBody: The AI says this came from the document, but the system could NOT find it word-for-word — treat it as the AI's own reasoning.
authoring.tbSourceNoneBody: This was generated by the AI from a topic, not drawn from your uploaded document — there is no verbatim line for you to check against.
authoring.tbStructCoveragePass: This objective is measured by at least one small piece of knowledge — it isn't left empty.
authoring.tbStructCoverageFail: Nothing currently measures this objective — needs another look.
authoring.tbOverridden: The reviewer decided differently from the machine.
authoring.tbTitleConcept: Why this piece of knowledge exists
authoring.tbTitleCoverage: Why this objective needs that knowledge
authoring.tbTitleIdentity: Why these two were treated as one
authoring.tbTitleProposed: The book teaches something the framework does not list
authoring.tbReasonTitle: The machine's own account — needs a person to confirm
authoring.tbEmptyAny: No evidence stored for this yet — import from a document, or run the sample data.
authoring.tbStructIdentityPass: This says plainly what it is about, so it cannot be confused with the one next to it.
authoring.tbStructIdentityFail: It doesn't say what it is about — two entries could be the same without the machine noticing.
authoring.tbStructOrderProven: The machine could check this: the narrower range sits inside the wider one, so the narrower comes first. Certain about range, not an absolute requirement.
authoring.tbStructOrderReversed: The order looks REVERSED — what is placed first is wider than what follows. Worth a second look.
authoring.tbStructOrderJudgment: The machine cannot prove this order; it is a teaching judgement and needs a teacher to confirm it.
authoring.tbStructRequiredAll: To count as met, every listed piece is required — miss one and it is not met.
authoring.tbStructRequiredMissing: This piece is no longer linked to the objective — what it measures has changed since review.
authoring.tbStructReadingPass: The document itself puts this one before the other. That is page order, not a teaching argument — but nothing contradicts it.
authoring.tbStructReadingFail: The document puts this one AFTER the other, the opposite of the order written down. Page order is not a teaching argument, but a contradiction is worth a look.
authoring.tbStructUnknown: The system recorded a self-check here, but there is no plain-language explanation for it yet.
authoring.tbStructNotRechecked: This is the result at review time; the system could not re-check it today.
authoring.tbSourceMachineTitle: Worked out by the machine, not quoted from a document
authoring.tbSourceMachineBody: There is no line in a document for you to check against: the system worked this out itself — this is not the AI guessing.
authoring.tbNewerGeneration: This is the newest version; {n} older ones from earlier imports.
authoring.tbOpenDoc: Open the document at the exact line (page {page})
authoring.relProven: Machine-checked: the smaller fits inside the larger → the smaller is usually learned first. Certain about the range (not an absolute must).
authoring.relContradicted: ⚠ The order looks BACKWARDS — the earlier one is wider than the later one. Worth another look.
authoring.relJudgment: The machine can't prove this order (different objects, or the ranges aren't comparable). It's only sure the learning chain doesn't loop. Why one comes first is the author's/AI's pedagogical judgment — please confirm.
authoring.relMapping: This objective is MEASURED by that knowledge. The machine checks: all of the knowledge is required to count as met — miss one and it isn't. Why exactly these pieces is the author's/AI's call — please confirm.
authoring.relLateral: A related link set by the author/AI — not a required learning order.
authoring.crosswalkPageDesc: Studied one programme and moving to another — what carries over, and what's still to learn.
authoring.crosswalkPickTwo: Pick two different frameworks to compare.
authoring.crosswalkNoGap: Nothing missing — the source framework already covers all of it.
authoring.crosswalkZoneTarget: Only the new one — to learn
authoring.crosswalkPartialHint: Partial: some of the concepts an objective needs are held, but not all — the risky case, since an objective counts as met only when every concept is.
authoring.planCourseSubtitle: Goals, outcomes, pedagogy, unit sequence, assessment strategy
authoring.planUnitSubtitle: Learning arc, unit objectives, per-lesson roles, unit assessment
authoring.planGateCourse: Approve the course plan first to generate unit plans.
authoring.planBigIdeaCourse: Big Idea — enduring understanding across the course
authoring.planBigIdeaUnit: Big Idea — enduring understanding of the unit
authoring.jobBackground: Runs in the background — reloading keeps it going.
authoring.csNoArcs: This lesson plan has no step structure yet.
authoring.csNoBrief: No brief — content may be generic
authoring.csAudioAfterApprove: Approve the text first to generate audio
authoring.fwNoMarks: no identifying marks yet — cannot be told apart from other knowledge
authoring.colTitle: Two pieces of knowledge the machine cannot tell apart ({n})
authoring.colIntro: The machine compared every identifying mark and found them all the same, so it will not merge on its own: merging wrongly damages the evidence trail for good, without raising an error. Two genuinely different pieces of knowledge can still match on every mark — so this one needs a teacher to settle.
authoring.colAllSame: The same on all {n} marks that could be compared — the machine has nothing left to tell them apart by.
authoring.colMergeHint: Which one stays? The other passes all its relations and objectives over to the one you keep.
authoring.colDistinguish: They are TWO — say what differs
authoring.colDistinguishHint: Pick the mark that differs, then give the second one its new value.
authoring.colClear: Nothing left that the machine is stuck on — ready to write.
authoring.colRejected: {n} decisions could not be carried out (target gone, or left blank).
authoring.colNotKnowledge: Not something to teach — take it out
authoring.colNotKnowledgeHint: A section heading, a lead-in sentence or a general habit of mind is not something a child learns and is measured on. Say why you are taking it out: someone will later ask why the framework does not have it.
authoring.cycTitle: The learning order loops back on itself ({n})
authoring.cycIntro: This must be learnt before that, and that must be learnt before this. There is nowhere to start, so the order cannot be used. The machine can see the loop but cannot see which link is wrong — taken one at a time, every link looks fine. Break the weakest link: leave the ones the machine can prove.
authoring.cycProven: the machine can prove this order
authoring.cycJudged: a judgement, with nothing backing it yet
authoring.cycCaveat: the reasoning holds, but nothing behind it was checked against the document
authoring.xwWhyTitle: Why they differ — {n} pieces of knowledge on one side only
authoring.xwWhyIntro: On one side only does not mean the other side is missing something. Most of the time it is the same thing at a different range, or learnt through a different channel. Each entry below is paired with its closest counterpart, along with what makes them different.
authoring.xwNoCounterpart: Nothing on the other side to compare against.
authoring.xwScopeSubset: narrower — coming from this side, the upper range is still missing
authoring.xwScopeSuperset: wider — covers the other side and more
authoring.pgNoConcepts: This lesson is not linked to any knowledge — nothing to trace back to.
authoring.pgNoObjectives: No objective in any framework asks for this knowledge. The lesson can still be taught, but it certifies nothing.
authoring.pgContextOk: The course and unit plans are approved, so this lesson was written from them.
authoring.pgContextMissing: The course or unit plan is not approved — a lesson written now has nothing to anchor to.
authoring.tbRejectNeedsNote: To say it is wrong, give a reason.
authoring.cwResetApproval: The approval on this course shell was removed
authoring.cwResetApprovalBody: Someone had approved a course shell under this same name, and this run replaced its content outright. The earlier approval no longer describes anything, so the status is back to draft — work nobody has read must not carry the mark of someone who read something else.
authoring.tbAcceptHint: Say what it is ABOUT and how it is PERFORMED. Without those two, the machine cannot later tell it apart from the entry beside it, and that kind of mix-up cannot be undone.

learn.title: Learn
learn.subtitle: The learning surface across 5 axes — pick a config and format, mock content.

mock.s1Para: When a column's sum exceeds 9, we 'carry' 1 to the tens column. This is the core idea of multi-digit addition.
mock.s2Quote: Add the ones first: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 carry 1.
mock.s3ImgCap: Bundles of ten and loose sticks show the 'carry 1'.
mock.s4Callout: Always start from the ones column.

rich.cPara: When a column's sum exceeds 9, we 'carry' 1 to the left column. This is the core idea of multi-digit addition.
rich.cTermDef: The 1 that moves to the tens column when ones reach 10.
rich.cMathCap: Add the ones first, then the tens.
rich.weNote: Always start from the ones column.
rich.quoteText: Maths isn't hard when you break it into small steps.
rich.st1b: Ones under ones, tens under tens.
rich.imgCap: Bundles of ten and loose sticks show the 'carry 1'.
rich.acc1b: Because we keep 1 ten to add in the next column.
rich.acc2b: When each column's sum is below 10.
rich.dlg1t: Why does the ones column become 12?
rich.dlgQ: So where does the carried 1 go?
rich.psg1: Long ago, whenever the ones column filled to 10, a tiny '1' climbed to the tens column.
rich.psg2: Thanks to it, big sums always came out right.
rich.expQ: Will the wooden ball float or sink?
rich.expS1: Drop the wooden ball in water
rich.disPrompt: Discuss: when does addition need carrying?
rich.lyr1: Add the ones, over ten they go
rich.lyr2: Carry a little one, to the next row
rich.lyr3: Add the tens plus one, and we're done
